title: Picket-fence latency probe — exploratory notes
content:
Purpose:
- Quick exploratory scratchpad to capture 'picket-fence' arrival pattern behavior.
- Pattern: short periodic bursts (3–8 requests every 200ms) separated by idle windows (2–4s). Emulates a polling UI that does short batched calls then idles.

Environment / harness:
- Branch: local harness vs. dedicated stager (pull/infra/412).
- Model: llama-v2-7b-quant (q4_0), KV cache enabled.
- Runtime: 4xA10g equivalent nodes behind router; continuous batching enabled with max_batch=48, batch_timeout_ms=8 (default).
- Client: python bench client (simple asyncio driver), recording per-request trace with server-side timestamps.
- Metrics collected: request latency (end-to-end), server queue wait, batch size at inference, KV cache hit/miss, GPU util.

Test matrix (notes):
- P1: Short bursts of 5 requests at 200ms spacing, idle 3s, for 10 minutes. (baseline)
- P2: Same burst size but reduce idle to 1s (higher duty).
- P3: Increase burst size to 12, spacing 100ms, idle 4s (fatter bursts).
- P4: Cold-start validation: clear model shard cache + restart node, run P1. Repeat twice.

Raw summary (aggregated run summaries) — approximate values, sampled from traces:
- P1 (5 req/200ms, idle3s): overall QPS ~0.8; mean p50=32ms, p95=96ms, p99=210ms, p999=410ms; batch size distribution: 60% single, 30% 2-4, 10% >4. KV cache hit: ~72%. GPU util baseline: 23%.
- P2 (5 req/200ms, idle1s): QPS ~2.4; p50=34ms, p95=120ms, p99=290ms, p999=520ms; batch size: 40% single, 40% 2-8, 20%>8. KV hit: 65%. GPU util: 47%.
- P3 (12 req/100ms, idle4s): QPS ~2.9 (bursts packed); p50=38ms, p95=130ms, p99=360ms, p999=780ms (long tail during heavy bursts). Batch size: 25% single, 25% 2-6, 50%>8. KV hit: 78% (higher since repeated context). GPU util: 49%.
- P4 (cold): initial 90s window shows p50=120ms, p95=540ms, p99=1.8s, then converges to P1 baseline after warmup.

Observations / quick hypotheses:
1) "Picket-fence" style bursts produce a bimodal batch size distribution: many singletons (requests that hit an empty batch window) + large-packed batches once queues accumulate. This produces moderate mean latency but heavy p99/p999 tails.
2) Idle windows allow the KV cache to remain warm if the idle < ~5s for repeated keys. Longer idle windows (>=60s in a separate run) cause cold misses and much worse tails.
3) Batch_timeout_ms=8ms seems too aggressive for small periodic bursts: we see many singletons. Increasing timeout to 20–30ms reduced singleton fraction significantly in a short test (p95 improved ~15%), but increased p50 slightly (~+6ms). Tradeoff looks acceptable for this workload.
4) Duty cycle matters more than burst size for tail behavior: same average QPS but spikier distribution -> worse p99.
5) Cold-starts dominate very long tails; warmup heuristics (keep-alive hotpool for 2m) or small standby batchers could mitigate.

Quick experiments I ran interactively (notes):
- bump batch_timeout_ms to 30, rerun P1 (5 min): singleton rate dropped from 60% to 18%; p95 went from 96ms -> 82ms; p999 reduced from 410ms -> ~220ms. GPU util +4%.
- enable small request coalescer (client-side jitter of 6ms to align arrivals): reduced variance; p99 improved ~20% in most runs; but requires client changes (not always feasible).
- trial of conservative prefill: when idle window ends, send a lightweight keepalive probe to warm KV cache (1 token probe). Reduced early-burst p99 by ~30%. Cost: +0.03 QPS steady.

Representative ascii timeline (single 30s capture, timestamps removed):
[burst start]
req@0ms -> latency 28ms (single)
req@200ms -> latency 31ms (single)
req@400ms -> latency 30ms (single)
req@600ms -> latency 95ms (batched, 3x)
... idle 3s ...
[burst]
req@0ms -> 26ms
req@200ms -> 120ms (cold miss during first few requests)

Open questions / next tests:
- How does model size affect the singleton vs pack tradeoff? Run same pattern against 2.7B / 13B quant variants.
- Evaluate adaptive batch_timeout: increase timeout when detecting bursts to capture trailing arrivals, decrease during steady-state. Could be simple heuristic: observed inter-arrival < 300ms for last N requests -> increase timeout to 30ms for next T sec.
- SLO angle: if product SLO is p95<100ms, these picket patterns are borderline; need either client-side coalescing, a small admission buffer (short delay), or runtime adapt batch_timeout.
- Cost calculus: keepalive probes reduce tail but add tokens/requests; quantify per-100k users.

TODO (practical):
- [ ] Run P1/P2/P3 against 2.7B and 13B quant variants (quick 20m runs) — schedule Wed morning.
- [ ] Implement a conservative adaptive batch_timeout prototype in runtime (toggle flag) and run A/B. (PR infra/416?)
- [ ] Add a lightweight 'probe warm' feature: optional tiny token probe that primes KV cache per-tenant after idle window > 1s. Measure token overhead.
- [ ] Draft a short note for product with recommendations (p99 risk + mitigation options).

Notes-to-self:
- Watch for sampling bias: earlier harness had an implicit client-side jitter (random seed) which masked singleton rate. Make sure deterministic inter-arrival in main runs.
- Remember to export per-request trace with batch_id so we can correlate which requests were batched together (helps root-cause p999).

Bottom line (current thinking):
- For polling/picket-style UIs, slightly increasing server batch timeout (20–30ms) + optional tiny keepalives gives a good latency-tail vs cost tradeoff. Adaptive batching would be ideal for mixed workloads.
